review.verdict: A clean, cheap run (2 workflows, 70 of 100 budget, 0 refusals, 9 of 9 done-when items passing), but an easy test that barely exercised the conflict machinery, and the department kept talking after it was done.

identity.note: Clear handoff to Adaptation [4] and a well-evidenced done verdict [16]. It bundled three questions into one CEO ask [2]. At [20] it told Adaptation and Priority to propose nothing and leave the 30 unspent, which is outside its decision list. [23] repeats [16].

adaptation.note: Small plan with extras skipped [6]. It declined an 8-cost fix for a warning that did not fail done-when [19]. Proposal fields (completion check, risks) are not visible in chat, so they cannot be verified. [21] re-announces a no-op.

priority.note: GRANT with rate-card math, opportunity cost and a stop-loss [7]. It never had to counter, so bargaining is untested. Envelope fields are not shown in chat.

coordination.note: Stated the rule and the dependency reason both times [9][11]. Only one order was possible, so the HOLD and collision paths were not tested.

audit.note: Mechanical check plus 9 items, one real low warning, correct handoff to Identity [14][15]. The chat shows no per-item evidence, so 'all pass' cannot be checked from the log.

ceo.note: One option per question, a one-line reason each, trade-off named, and it said the brief was silent [3]. It picked Identity's first-listed option 3 of 3 times. n=3 is too thin to call that bias.

builder.note: Did what was declared, in order. The file is 19.5 KB with no JS errors and no overflow [10][12][14]. It added an optional date field, disclosed in [12]; minor.

went_well: No validator refusals, role refusals, redirects, invalid moves or stuck turns. The charter passed on the first try [5].
The CEO's three choices flowed into the charter, the plan and the verdict. The 'structure complete, not publishable' trade-off was stated at each step [3][6][16].
Open inputs never blocked done, and no prices or invented facts appear in the charter or the audit result.
Code-run mechanical checks (360px and 1280px overflow, JS errors, broken links) backed Audit's judgment [14].
problems: 4 of 15 agent turns came after done was declared [19][20][21][23]. They added no new information, and Identity's [23] repeats [16].
Counters, conflicts, HOLDs, rework and Requester pauses were all 0. Negotiation, conflict resolution and the audit-rework loop were not tested.
Estimate equals charged on both workflows (35/35) because of the rate card. That says nothing about how well estimates track real cost.
The chat shows the chosen option as 'Option 2' in all three questions [2][3], but the log says original position 0. I cannot tell which order the CEO saw, so the position-bias numbers are unreliable.
Identity says the hero headline is 'listed in the swap guide' [16]. Nothing in the log verifies that.
Done-when checks are mostly presence checks. Nothing tests whether the photos carry the page or the design reads as editorial, and 'Looks good' [18] is a weak approval signal.
learnings: Close by code when the Requester approves with no change. It would have saved the 4 turns after [18]. The cost is that Adaptation gets no last look for gaps.

Allow bundled CEO questions and update identity.md to say so. Three questions in one ask cost one CEO call and worked [2][3]. This is a decision for the role file, since the file currently says one bounded decision.
Run a harder brief next: a tight budget so Priority must counter, and a done-when item that forces rework. Without that, every negotiation metric stays at zero.
Charge measured cost, or vary the rate card, if estimate accuracy is meant to be tested. A fixed card makes estimate_vs_charged meaningless.
Test CEO position bias properly: repeat across several runs, vary which option Identity lists first, and fix the chat/log order mismatch before trusting identity_first.
Log Audit's per-item verdicts and the proposal and envelope fields in the chat or event log so a reviewer can verify them. Add a screenshot or visual check for the 'photo-led, editorial' item.
